newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pilots call Thursday strike at Air France Europe.
newsitem.headline: Pilots call Thursday strike at Air France Europe.

text.p: Air France Europe said pilots had called a snap 24-hour strike for Thursday and that all flights would be cancelled except those to the island of Corsica and a limited number to three French towns from Paris.

Air France Europe, the domestic and short-haul division of Air France, issued a statement condemning the strike called by several unions as "suicidal" and saying it would not give in to "blackmail" from the best paid pilots in the world.

The pilots, protesting against plans for a full merger with parent company Air France, had cost the airline more than a billion francs through industrial action over the past five years, the airline said.
It said it would try to ensure one in three flights between Paris Orly airport and Marseille, Toulouse and Strasbourg.
The strike runs from midnight on Wednesday (2300 GMT).
"This strike, the 41st in two years, is even more disastrous because the pilots of Air France Europe have made it impossible for the company to warn its customers," the airline said.

"The pilots of Air France Europe have the best conditions of all world airlines. They cost twice as much per flying hour as their counterparts at British Airways and ... 30 percent more than at (parent) Air France," it added.
A similar snap strike by pilots grounded flights to all destinations except the French Mediterranean island of Corsica on February 9.
